name: Ultramarine Blue
note: The workhorse blue. Separates beautifully against burnt sienna in a wet wash.

name: Phthalo Blue GS
note: A cold, staining blue with enormous tinting strength. A little goes a long way in a mix.

name: Cerulean Blue
note: Chalky and opaque next to the other blues. Sits on the surface rather than sinking into the paper.

name: Indanthrone Blue
note: Darker and less green than ultramarine, with a quiet granulation that only shows in heavier washes.

name: Viridian
note: A cool, muted green that breaks into soft textured passages. Rarely garish, even at full strength.

name: Phthalo Green BS
note: Extremely staining and near black in mass tone. Dilutes to a clear, cold green.

name: Nickel Azo Yellow
note: A deep, transparent gold yellow that glazes cleanly over darker colours without muddying them.

name: Hansa Yellow Light
note: Bright and clean, but the weakest lightfastness in the range at Blue Wool 6. Keep finished work out of direct sun.

name: Beitou Sulphur
note: Ground from mineral deposits in the Beitou geothermal valley. Granulates harder than anything else in the range, with no synthetic equivalent.

name: Yellow Ochre
note: Earthy and forgiving, with heavy natural granulation. A dependable base for skin and stone.

name: Raw Sienna
note: Lighter and more transparent than yellow ochre, with a warm amber cast in thin washes.

name: Burnt Sienna
note: The other half of the ultramarine granulating mix. Warm, heavy, and unshakeably reliable.

name: Pyrrol Scarlet
note: A clean, opaque-leaning red with none of the staining problems of the older cadmium substitutes.

name: Quinacridone Rose
note: Intensely staining and transparent, with a cool undertone that reads closer to magenta than red.

name: Perylene Maroon
note: A deep, near-black red that stays warm rather than turning muddy in shadow mixes.

name: Cobalt Violet
note: Soft, chalky, and very heavily granulating. One of the few true violets that is not a mixed pigment.

name: Yushan Slate
note: Ground from slate collected in the Yushan range. A cool, zero-staining grey with very heavy granulation.

name: Payne's Grey
note: The one mix in the range, built from lamp black and ultramarine. Labelled as a mix because it is one.
